A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original GRU, LSTM, and Transformer training experiments, causal interventions, task accuracies, and interchange intervention accuracies in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds an Increment-Up comparison, a GRU subspace-size experiment, and PCA case studies.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the stated linear-alignment parameterization from X = SMM^T to X = (MM^T + epsilon I)S, with epsilon = 0.1, adding stabilization and changing where the diagonal scaling acts. The core alignment and intervention framework remains. This establishes a reported parameterization revision, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The Multi-Object, Single-Object, Same-Object, Variable-Length, and simplified counting settings are retained. v3's simplified Multi-Object description still uses one demonstration-token type and omits BOS/T, matching v2's simplified Single-Object setting. The added analyses use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Increment-Up as a negative baseline in Appendix A.3 and Figure 15, comparing its Progress variable with Up-Down's Count under orthogonal and linear alignments for Multi-Object and Same-Object GRUs. Existing comparison algorithms are retained.

E3.justification: New Figure 9 evaluates orthogonal GRU alignments at subspace sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 16, 32, and 64. The added PCA analyses use 15 trials per quantity from 1–20. These introduce settings for additional analyses; the original splits, task metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnosis of alignment behavior: PCA contrasts Multi-Object and Same-Object GRU trajectories, the Increment-Up control tests whether flexible alignment succeeds for an alternative algorithm, and Figure 9 extends orthogonal subspace-size sensitivity to GRUs. These additions directly investigate the interpretation and selectivity of LAF alignment.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 newly specifies that excluded low-accuracy seeds were not replaced, and the added baseline and PCA analyses explicitly identify their single-seed basis. The original five-seed training plan and retained uncertainty displays are unchanged; no increased replication or new statistical testing is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the retained plots are unchanged. Added findings include Increment-Up IIA of 58.1% for Same-Object with OAF, and 72.2%/89.4% for Multi-Object/Same-Object with LAF, plus new sensitivity and PCA results. v3's broad >95% GRU Up-Up wording is imprecise relative to Table 1's retained Multi-Object values of 91.74% and 92.23%.

T1.justification: Section 4.1.5 corrects the component partition in Equations 8–9, starting the retained target components at dvar + 1, and adds blockwise derivations concerning relationships among aligned variables in Equations 10–11. The anti-Markovian theorem and proof are unchanged, moving from Appendix A.6 to A.7.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain, but v3 explicitly includes alignment failures in the abstract and replaces v2's concluding assertion that poor alignment simply requires refining the symbolic algorithm with a more conditional account of approximate learned algorithms. This modestly qualifies the scope of the interpretability claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1.1 now distinguishes recovering causally controllable variables through an LAF from establishing that a network possesses distinct variables implementing a particular algorithm. It warns that high LAF accuracy can fit conceptually different programs. The rewritten conclusion also substantively limits extrapolation from the models' narrow training experience to richer cognition.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly describes teacher-forced training, explains the existing quantity range, holdouts, and 99% selection threshold, and documents the revised LAF construction. Appendix A.3 and Algorithm 4 provide implementation details for Increment-Up. These are limited documentation additions; the existing hardware and main training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Related Work substantially expands positioning against program compilation and synthesis, modular-addition interpretability, neuroscience mapping models, and representation-shape metrics, including Lindner, Michaud, Nanda, Ivanova, and Williams. Additional human-number and graded-state-machine references also contextualize the interpretations and conclusion.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and the recurrent-results narrative is reorganized around numeric neural variables before individual-neuron interventions. Alignment explanation and visualization become separate subsections. OAF/LAF terminology, expanded explanations, and new appendix sections produce substantial editorial restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 adds four figures covering GRU subspace sensitivity, Increment-Up comparisons, and two PCA visualizations, plus Algorithm 4. Existing Figures 3 and 4 exchange order, Figure 8 is enlarged, and publication headers and figure placement change. Existing plots and result-table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The Increment-Up control, PCA evidence, and clearer distinction between causal control and identifying a learned algorithm improve the paper's interpretive rigor. Documentation and mathematical corrections also help. The gain is limited by the single-seed basis of the new diagnostic evidence and imprecise >95% wording relative to Table 1; the principal empirical results and transformer proof remain unchanged.
